Step-Back Supported Split Squat to High Box (short ROM)
Tall-Kneeling Pallof Press (band) or DB Press-Out iso
Hip Hinge to Mid-Shin with Light DBs (RDL pattern)
Goblet Squat (to or just above box)
Bird Dog (longer lever if no coning)
Push-Up Eccentric to Floor (slow lowers; press up from knees or incline as needed)
Split Squat (with 1–2s pause at bottom, light goblet)
One-Arm DB Row (2s pause at top)
Hip Thrust (shoulders on couch, light DB on hips)
Single-Leg RDL (supported, bodyweight or light DB)
Suitcase Carry Offset (heavier DB one side)
Squat Complex: Goblet Squats + Squat Iso Holds
Dead-bug arm reaches with exhale brace
Low step pogo (intro in Week 5+ if cleared)
Jump rope “ghost” line hops (intro in Week 5+ if cleared)

notes: Frequency: 3 strength sessions per week plus 2 low-impact cardio or active recovery days and 1 full rest day
Session length 30–45 minutes
Emphasis on breath-coordinated bracing; exhale on exertion; avoid doming/coning
Stop or modify if pain, pressure, heaviness, bulging, or leaking
Progression: increase load first, then volume; regress if symptoms arise
No jumping or impact; use tempo, pauses, and step variations as substitutes
Warm-up each session 5–8 minutes following template
Cool-down 3–5 minutes with downregulation breathing and gentle stretches
Brisk walks at conversational pace on cardio days; focus on posture and arm swing
Reduce ROM, slow tempo, or lighten load if pain/pressure in pelvis or low back
Inhale to set; exhale and gently lift pelvic floor during effort; relax between reps
Week 2 add 5–10 lb to goblet squat if Week 1 felt easy
Optional low-impact circuit in Week 2 at easy pace for 10–12 minutes
Week 3 optional incline walking intervals 3–4 x 3 minutes at RPE 6 with 2 minutes easy
Week 4 carry finisher: farmer 60–75s, rest 60s, suitcase 45s per side
Daily 5-minute pelvic floor and core practice
Red flags to stop or modify include heaviness, leaking, doming, sharp pain, or delayed deep pelvic soreness
Sleep target 7–9 hours across 24 hours; if sleep-poor keep intensity at RPE 5–6
Hydration ~2–3 L/day; more if breastfeeding
If all readiness criteria met after Week 4, introduce low-amplitude impact in Week 5+ or transition to preferred training style
For diastasis: keep head and shoulders down in supine core, emphasize anti-extension and anti-rotation, avoid long-lever flexion until tension is good
For C-section scar discomfort: shorten ROM on deep hinge/prone and add more glute bridges/hip thrusts

raw_text:
Here’s a 4-week, home-based on-ramp block designed for a 10-weeks-postpartum client cleared for moderate exercise, with a no-jumping restriction for the next 4 weeks. It prioritizes core and pelvic floor integrity, gradual strength reintroduction, and aerobic base without impact. Equipment: bodyweight, light dumbbells (5–15 lb range), chair/bench, mini-band (optional), yoga strap/towel.

Global notes
- Frequency: 3 strength sessions/week + 2 low-impact cardio/active recovery days. 1 full rest day.
- Session length: 30–45 minutes.
- Intensity: RPE 5–7 (challenging but controlled), leave 2–3 reps in reserve.
- Core/pelvic floor: Emphasis on breath-coordinated bracing, no doming/coning. Exhale on exertion. Stop/modify if pain, pressure, heaviness, bulging, or leaking.
- Progression: Increase load first, then volume. If symptoms arise, hold at current level or regress 1 step.
- Walking guidelines: Start where comfortable; build by ~10%/week.
- No jumping/impact: Substitute with tempo, pauses, and step variations.

Structure overview
- Week 1: Acclimatisation and reconnection. Restore breathing mechanics, gentle core, foundational movement patterns, short sessions.
- Week 2: Build consistency and time-under-tension. Light dumbbells, controlled tempos.
- Week 3: Load and range. Add split stance, hinge depth, light carries.
- Week 4: Baseline consolidation. Slight volume bump, introduce complexes, prep for next phase.

Warm-up template (all weeks, 5–8 minutes)
- 1–2 minutes diaphragmatic breathing: Supine or 90/90, inhale 3–4s into ribs, exhale 4–6s, gentle pelvic floor lift on exhale, relax fully on inhale.
- 1 minute spinal/rib mobility: Open books x6/side, cat-cow x6.
- 1–2 minutes dynamic prep: Hip airplanes (supported) x5/side, ankle rocks x10, shoulder circles x10.
- 1 minute activation: Glute bridge iso 20–30s, dead bug arms-only x6/side with breath.

Cool-down (3–5 minutes)
- Box breathing or 4–7–8 breathing for downregulation.
- Gentle hip flexor stretch, pec doorway stretch, calves.

WEEK 1: Acclimatisation and reconnection
Goal: Re-establish routine, breathing, pelvic floor coordination, and basic strength with low total volume.

Strength Sessions (3x/week, nonconsecutive)

Session A
- Box Sit-to-Stand (chair height), 3x8, tempo 3–1–2, exhale up.
- Supported Incline Push-Up (hands on countertop/bench), 3x6–8.
- Hip Hinge Drill with Dowel/Wall Tap, 3x8 controlled.
- Side-Lying Clamshell (mini-band optional), 2x10/side.
- Dead Bug (legs table-top, alternating arms), 2x6/side; stop if coning.
- Farmer Carry March (light DBs), 3x20–30s, ribs stacked, slow march.

Session B
- Step-Back Supported Split Squat to High Box (short ROM), 3x6/side.
- One-Arm DB Row (support on bench), 3x8/side, 2–3s eccentric.
- Glute Bridge, 3x8, 2s pause at top.
- Tall-Kneeling Pallof Press (band) or DB Press-Out iso, 3x10s holds x5 reps/side.
- Heel Slides with Exhale Brace, 2x6/side.
- Standing Calf Raise, 2x12, slow.

Session C
- Goblet Squat to Box (light DB), 3x6–8, tempo 3–1–2.
- Half-Kneeling Overhead Press (light DB), 3x6/side.
- Hip Hinge to Mid-Shin with Light DBs (RDL pattern), 3x8.
- Side Plank (knees), 3x15–20s/side, neutral ribcage.
- Bird Dog (short lever), 2x6/side.
- Carry Option: Suitcase Carry (one DB), 3x20–30s/side.

Cardio/Active Recovery (2 days)
- Brisk walk 20–30 minutes, conversational pace. Optional stroller pushes, focus on posture and arm swing.

Notes/Checks
- No pain/pressure in pelvis or low back. If present, reduce ROM, slow tempo, or lighten load.
- Breath cue: inhale to set, exhale and gently lift PF during the effort; fully relax between reps.

WEEK 2: Consistency and controlled load
Goal: Slight volume increase and introduce light DB loading where tolerated.

Strength Sessions (3x/week)

Session A
- Goblet Squat (to or just above box), 4x6–8, add 5–10 lb if Week 1 felt easy.
- Incline Push-Up (lower surface slightly if symptom-free), 4x6–8.
- DB RDL, 3x8–10, 2–3s eccentric.
- Side-Lying Clamshell or Banded Monster Walk, 2x12–15.
- Dead Bug (opposite arm/leg), 3x5/side.
- Farmer Carry March, 3x30–40s.

Session B
- Split Squat (rear foot on floor), 3x6–8/side, bodyweight or light goblet hold.
- One-Arm DB Row, 4x8–10/side.
- Glute Bridge March, 3x8/side, slow.
- Tall-Kneeling Pallof Press, 3x8–10/side, 2s hold out front.
- Standing Calf Raise, 3x12–15, add load if tolerated.

Session C
- Reverse Lunge to Box Tap (control depth), 3x6–8/side.
- Half-Kneeling DB Overhead Press, 3x8/side.
- Hip Hinge: KB/DB Romanian Deadlift, 4x8.
- Side Plank (knees or staggered feet), 3x20–25s/side.
- Bird Dog (longer lever if no coning), 3x6/side.
- Suitcase Carry, 3x30–40s/side.

Cardio/Active Recovery
- 2 sessions of 25–35 minutes brisk walking or low-incline treadmill.
- Optional: 1 low-impact circuit (10–12 minutes): mini-band lateral walks 30s, step-ups 30s/side (no jump), standing wall push endurance 30s, repeat 2–3 rounds at easy pace.

WEEK 3: Load and range progression
Goal: Increase range in squats/hinges, introduce tempo/pauses, add unilateral stability and carries. Still no impact.

Strength Sessions (3x/week)

Session A
- Front-Loaded Squat (goblet), 4x8, full depth within control; 1–0–2 tempo.
- Push-Up Eccentric to Floor (knees up or down), 3x6 slow lowers + press up from knees or incline, as needed.
- DB RDL, 4x8–10, add load if grip/Achilles allow.
- Curtsy or Lateral Lunge (short range to start), 3x6/side.
- Dead Bug with Band Press-Out (anti-extension), 3x6/side.
- Farmer Carry Continuous (both DBs), 3x40–50s.

Session B
- Split Squat (add 1–2s pause at bottom), 4x6–8/side, light goblet.
- One-Arm DB Row with 2s pause at top, 4x8/side.
- Hip Thrust (shoulders on couch, light DB on hips), 3x10, 2s squeeze.
- Half-Kneeling Anti-Rotation Press (Pallof), 3x10/side.
- Standing Single-Leg Calf Raise holding support, 3x10/side.

Session C
- Step-Up to Knee Drive (control, no hop), 3x8/side, mid-height step.
- Half-Kneeling DB Arnold Press, 3x8/side.
- Single-Leg RDL (supported, bodyweight or light DB), 3x6–8/side.
- Side Plank (feet), 3x20–30s/side, regress if doming.
- Quadruped Hover (knees 1 inch off, 10–20s), 3 sets.
- Suitcase Carry Offset (heavier DB one side), 3x40s/side.

Cardio/Active Recovery
- 2 sessions of 30–40 minutes brisk walking or low-impact cardio (elliptical/spin if available, low resistance).
- Optional incline walking intervals: 3–4 x 3 minutes incline 3–5% at RPE 6, 2 minutes easy.

WEEK 4: Consolidate baseline and prep for next phase
Goal: Slight increase in intensity/complexity; introduce simple complexes and extended sets to build work capacity without impact.

Strength Sessions (3x/week)

Session A
- Squat Complex: 6 Goblet Squats + 6 Squat Iso Holds (20s total, e.g., 2x10s mid-range), 3 rounds, 60–90s rest.
- Push Progression: Incline Push-Up or Floor-Elevated Push-Up, 4x8–10.
- Hinge: DB RDL, 4x8–10, moderate load.
- Anti-Rotation Walkout (band) or Long-Lever Pallof, 3x8/side.
- Dead Bug to Toe Tap (light), 3x6/side.

Session B
- Split Squat Ladder: 8-6-6/side across 3 sets, small load increase; 1–1–2 tempo.
- Row: 3-Point DB Row, 4x10/side.
- Hip Thrust with 3s pause, 3x8–10.
- Single-Leg Glute Bridge, 3x8/side.
- Side Plank with Row (band) or Hip Abduction, 3x8/side.

Session C
- Step-Up Volume: 3x10/side, control down; no hop.
- Overhead Press Standing (bilateral DB), 4x8, brace and exhale.
- Single-Leg RDL (supported or free), 3x8/side, light–moderate load.
- Bear Crawl March (in place), 3x20–30s.
- Carry Finisher: Farmer 60–75s, rest 60s, Suitcase 45s/side.

Cardio/Active Recovery
- 2 sessions of 35–45 minutes walk/elliptical/spin at RPE 5–6.
- Optional sub-threshold intervals: 4 x 4 minutes at RPE ~6 with 2 minutes easy.

Pelvic floor and core guidelines
- Daily 5-minute practice:
  - 6–8 breath cycles: 360° breathing, full rib expansion, full pelvic floor relaxation on inhale, gentle 20–30% lift on exhale.
  - 2 sets: 5 dead-bug arm reaches with exhale brace; 5 heel slides with exhale brace.
  - Optional: side-lying hip release, adductor rock-backs for tension relief.
- Red flags to stop/modify: heaviness/pressure in vagina, urinary leaking, doming along midline, sharp low-back/pelvic pain, delayed soreness that feels “inside” pelvis.

General recovery
- Sleep: Aim for total 7–9 hours across 24 hours (naps count). If sleep-poor, keep intensity at RPE 5–6 that day.
- Walking posture: Tall, ribs over pelvis, gentle arm swing.
- Hydration: ~2–3 L/day, more if breastfeeding.
- Nutrition: Emphasize protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day if medically appropriate, evenly distributed; carbohydrate around workouts; calcium, vitamin D, iron and DHA per medical guidance. If breastfeeding, add ~300–500 kcal/day and prioritize fluids/electrolytes.
- DOMS management: Easy walks, gentle mobility, heat, and light self-massage. Avoid aggressive abdominal stretching early on.

Progression and readiness to advance after week 4
- She completes sessions without pelvic floor/core symptoms.
- RPE 6–7 with good form; leaves 1–2 reps in reserve on final sets.
- Can perform:
  - 3x10 goblet squats with moderate load
  - 3x8 split squats/side under control
  - 30–45s side plank without coning
  - 45–60s continuous farmer carry with stable trunk
- If all green, you can introduce low-amplitude impact in Week 5+ (e.g., low step pogo, jump rope “ghost” line hops) per clearance and tolerance, or transition to her preferred training style.

Modifications
- Diastasis concerns: keep head/shoulders down in supine core, emphasize anti-extension/anti-rotation (Pallof, carries), avoid long-lever flexion until tension is good.
- C-section scar: respect tissue—if any pulling or discomfort with deep hinge or prone, shorten ROM and add more glute bridges/hip thrusts until comfortable.

This 4-week block restores key patterns, builds tolerance to moderate loads, and sets a solid baseline for a return to pre-pregnancy training in the next phase.
